body.translated_text: <s>Mahāyānapathasādhanasaṅgraha</s> (Compendium of the Means of Accomplishing the <s>Mahāyāna</s> Path)

children.translated_text: Since they are the progenitors of all <s>Buddhas</s> of the past and so forth, they are like parents;
with devotion, to the <s>sādhana</s>-<s>dharmas</s> (practices of accomplishment), I bow joyfully with speech and mind. (1)
If one wishes to grasp the inconceivable, great, supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),
since <s>sādhana</s> (practice) is the culmination of <s>bodhi</s>, one should embrace the <s>sādhana</s> in its essence. (2)

children.text: sa ca triśaraṇaṃ gattvā nivārya sakalāśubhān /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the <s>triśaraṇa</s> (three refuges), and having warded off all unwholesome deeds,
one should embrace pure higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), the vehicle of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). (3)
Relying further on the whip, striking with the remembrance of death,
one should cross this path of <s>bhava</s> (existence) of great terror, and do so swiftly. (4)
Having reached the fearless <s>Buddha</s>-ground, established in the stage of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>),
taking up the <s>sattvasaṃvara</s> (vow for beings), and the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) and the rest — (5)
one should practice the conduct for beings likewise, the collection of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means);
one should train in non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>; its essence is likewise twofold. (6)
Free from <s>rāga</s> (passion) and hostility, always desiring the fire, like the fire-drill,

children.text: bhāvayet satataṃ bhaktyā buddhaḥ śīghraṃ tato bhavet // 7 //
children.translated_text: one should constantly meditate with devotion; then one will swiftly become a <s>Buddha</s>. (7)
For the benefit of others, like a wish-fulfilling gem, he constantly acts without deliberate effort;
the fortunate ones should study this <s>Sādhanasaṅgraha</s> (Compendium of Practices) of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. (8)

children.text: cittaṃ sudhālavaiḥ raktaṃ buddhayśuddhau ca duḥspṛśam /
children.translated_text: The mind, stained with drops of nectar, is hard to touch in the purity of <s>Buddhahood</s>;
by the merit of this compendium, may the world proceed on the great path! (9)

body.text: buddhabhūmimahaṃ cāptvā bhaveyaṃ lokanāyakaḥ // 10 a ba //
body.translated_text: And may I, having attained the <s>Buddhabhūmi</s> (ground of Buddhahood), become a guide of the world! (10)
The 'Exceedingly Concise <s>Mahāyānapathasādhana</s>' composed by the great master <s>Dīpaṅkaraśrījñāna</s> is completed.

body.text: bhāratasya tenaiva upādhyāya-paṇḍitena lokacakṣuṣā bhikṣuṇā kalyāṇamatinā (dge vahi blo gros) ca anūdya nirṇītam //
body.translated_text: Translated and established by that same Indian preceptor-<s>paṇḍita</s>, the eye of the world, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Kalyāṇamati</s> (Tibetan: <s>dGe ba'i blo gros</s>).
